@@ -0,0 +1,111 @@
+package config
+
+import "time"
+
+// OS family identifiers used throughout scanning and lifecycle lookup.
+const (
+	RedHat                = "redhat"
+	Debian                = "debian"
+	Ubuntu                = "ubuntu"
+	CentOS                = "centos"
+	Fedora                = "fedora"
+	Amazon                = "amazon"
+	Oracle                = "oracle"
+	FreeBSD               = "freebsd"
+	Raspbian              = "raspbian"
+	Windows               = "windows"
+	OpenSUSE              = "opensuse"
+	OpenSUSELeap          = "opensuse.leap"
+	SUSEEnterpriseServer  = "suse.linux.enterprise.server"
+	SUSEEnterpriseDesktop = "suse.linux.enterprise.desktop"
+	SUSEOpenstackCloud    = "suse.openstack.cloud"
+	Alpine                = "alpine"
+	// ServerTypePseudo is used for ServerInfo.Type and the result family.
+	ServerTypePseudo = "pseudo"
+)
+
+// EOL describes the support deadlines for an OS release. Ended explicitly
+// marks a release as ended even when no deadline is supplied.
+type EOL struct {
+	StandardSupportUntil time.Time
+	ExtendedSupportUntil time.Time
+	Ended                bool
+}
+
+// IsStandardSupportEnded reports whether standard support has ended.
+func (e EOL) IsStandardSupportEnded(now time.Time) bool {
+	return e.Ended || (!e.StandardSupportUntil.IsZero() && now.After(e.StandardSupportUntil))
+}
+
+// IsExtendedSuppportEnded reports whether extended support has ended.
+// The spelling is retained as part of the public interface.
+func (e EOL) IsExtendedSuppportEnded(now time.Time) bool {
+	return e.Ended || (!e.ExtendedSupportUntil.IsZero() && now.After(e.ExtendedSupportUntil))
+}
+
+// eolDates contains only releases for which lifecycle data is modeled.
+// The first date is standard support; an empty second date means no extended phase.
+var eolDates = map[string]map[string][2]string{
+	Amazon: {
+		"2018.03":   {"2023-06-30", "2023-06-30"},
+		"2 (Karoo)": {"2025-06-30", ""},
+	},
+	RedHat: {
+		"7": {"2024-06-30", ""},
+		"8": {"2029-05-31", ""},
+		"6": {"2020-11-30", "2024-06-30"},
+	},
+	CentOS: {
+		"7": {"2024-06-30", ""},
+		"8": {"2021-12-31", ""},
+		"6": {"2020-11-30", "2020-11-30"},
+	},
+	Oracle: {
+		"7": {"2024-06-30", ""},
+		"8": {"2029-05-31", ""},
+		"6": {"2021-03-31", "2022-03-31"},
+	},
+	Ubuntu: {
+		"18.04": {"2023-05-31", "2028-04-30"},
+		"14.04": {"2019-04-30", "2024-04-30"},
+		"14.10": {"2015-07-30", "2015-07-30"},
+		"21.04": {"2022-01-30", ""},
+	},
+	Debian: {
+		"9":  {"2022-06-30", ""},
+		"10": {"2024-06-30", ""},
+		"8":  {"2020-06-30", "2020-06-30"},
+	},
+	Alpine: {
+		"3.10": {"2021-05-30", ""},
+		"3.11": {"2021-11-30", ""},
+		"3.12": {"2022-05-30", ""},
+		"3.9":  {"2020-11-30", "2020-11-30"},
+	},
+	FreeBSD: {
+		"11": {"2021-09-30", "2021-09-30"},
+		"12": {"2023-12-31", ""},
+		"10": {"2019-10-30", "2019-10-30"},
+	},
+}
+
+// GetEOL retrieves lifecycle dates by exact family and release identifier.
+func GetEOL(family, release string) (EOL, bool) {
+	dates, found := eolDates[family][release]
+	if !found {
+		return EOL{}, false
+	}
+	e := EOL{StandardSupportUntil: mustEOLDate(dates[0])}
+	if dates[1] != "" {
+		e.ExtendedSupportUntil = mustEOLDate(dates[1])
+	}
+	return e, true
+}
+
+func mustEOLDate(value string) time.Time {
+	date, err := time.Parse("2006-01-02", value)
+	if err != nil {
+		panic(err)
+	}
+	return date
+}

+		{Debian, "9", "2022-06-30", ""},
+		{Debian, "10", "2024-06-30", ""},
+		{Debian, "8", "2020-06-30", "2020-06-30"},
+		{Alpine, "3.10", "2021-05-30", ""},
+		{Alpine, "3.11", "2021-11-30", ""},
+		{Alpine, "3.12", "2022-05-30", ""},
+		{Alpine, "3.9", "2020-11-30", "2020-11-30"},
+		{FreeBSD, "11", "2021-09-30", "2021-09-30"},
+		{FreeBSD, "12", "2023-12-31", ""},
+		{FreeBSD, "10", "2019-10-30", "2019-10-30"},
+	}
+	for _, c := range cases {
+		e, found := GetEOL(c.family, c.release)
+		if !found || e.StandardSupportUntil.Format("2006-01-02") != c.standard {
+			t.Errorf("%s %s: standard=%s found=%v", c.family, c.release, e.StandardSupportUntil, found)
+		}
+		if c.extended == "" && !e.ExtendedSupportUntil.IsZero() || c.extended != "" && e.ExtendedSupportUntil.Format("2006-01-02") != c.extended {
+			t.Errorf("%s %s: extended=%s", c.family, c.release, e.ExtendedSupportUntil)

+	for _, c := range []struct{ family, release string }{

+	} {
+		if _, found := GetEOL(c.family, c.release); found {
+			t.Errorf("unexpected mapping for %s %s", c.family, c.release)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func TestEOLBoundaries(t *testing.T) {
+	standard, _ := time.Parse("2006-01-02", "2021-09-30")
+	e := EOL{StandardSupportUntil: standard, ExtendedSupportUntil: standard}
+	if e.IsStandardSupportEnded(standard) || e.IsExtendedSuppportEnded(standard) {
+		t.Fatal("support must remain active at the deadline")
+	}
+	if !e.IsStandardSupportEnded(standard.Add(time.Nanosecond)) || !e.IsExtendedSuppportEnded(standard.Add(time.Nanosecond)) {
+		t.Fatal("support must end strictly after the deadline")
+	}
+	if (EOL{StandardSupportUntil: standard}).IsExtendedSuppportEnded(standard.AddDate(1, 0, 0)) {
+		t.Fatal("absent extended support deadline must not be treated as ended")
+	}
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,15 @@
+// Package version contains version parsing shared by config and util.
+package version
+
+import "strings"
+
+// Major returns the part before the first dot, after an optional epoch.
+func Major(value string) string {
+	if i := strings.IndexByte(value, ':'); i >= 0 {
+		value = value[i+1:]
+	}
+	if i := strings.IndexByte(value, '.'); i >= 0 {
+		value = value[:i]
+	}
+	return value
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,56 @@
+package scan
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/future-architect/vuls/config"
+	"github.com/future-architect/vuls/util"
+)
+
+// eolRelease maps detected OS release strings to lifecycle release identifiers.
+// GetEOL itself requires an exact identifier, so unmodeled releases stay unknown.
+func eolRelease(family, release string) string {
+	switch family {
+	case config.RedHat, config.CentOS, config.Oracle, config.Debian, config.FreeBSD:
+		return util.Major(release)
+	case config.Ubuntu, config.Alpine:
+		parts := strings.Split(release, ".")
+		if len(parts) > 2 {
+			return strings.Join(parts[:2], ".")
+		}
+	case config.Amazon:
+		if strings.HasPrefix(release, "2 (") && strings.HasSuffix(release, ")") {
+			return "2 (Karoo)"
+		}
+	}
+	return release
+}
+
+// eolWarnings evaluates an OS release at the supplied time. Messages have no
+// prefix here; the summary adds "Warning: " to each message when rendering.
+func eolWarnings(family, release string, now time.Time) []string {
+	if family == config.ServerTypePseudo || family == config.Raspbian {
+		return nil
+	}
+	eol, found := config.GetEOL(family, eolRelease(family, release))
+	if !found {
+		return []string{fmt.Sprintf("Failed to check EOL. Register the issue to https://github.com/future-architect/vuls/issues with the information in 'Family: %s Release: %s'", family, release)}
+	}
+	if eol.IsStandardSupportEnded(now) {
+		warnings := []string{"Standard OS support is EOL(End-of-Life). Purchase extended support if available or Upgrading your OS is strongly recommended."}
+		if !eol.ExtendedSupportUntil.IsZero() {
+			if eol.IsExtendedSuppportEnded(now) {
+				warnings = append(warnings, "Extended support is also EOL. There are many Vulnerabilities that are not detected, Upgrading your OS strongly recommended.")
+			} else {
+				warnings = append(warnings, fmt.Sprintf("Extended support available until %s. Check the vendor site.", eol.ExtendedSupportUntil.Format("2006-01-02")))
+			}
+		}
+		return warnings
+	}
+	if !now.AddDate(0, 3, 0).Before(eol.StandardSupportUntil) {
+		return []string{fmt.Sprintf("Standard OS support will be end in 3 months. EOL date: %s", eol.StandardSupportUntil.Format("2006-01-02"))}
+	}
+	return nil
+}

+package scan
+
+import (
+	"reflect"

+

+)
+
+func TestEOLWarnings(t *testing.T) {
+	date := func(s string) time.Time { v, _ := time.Parse("2006-01-02", s); return v }
+	cases := []struct {
+		family, release string
+		now             time.Time
+		want            []string
+	}{
+		{config.Ubuntu, "14.10", date("2016-01-01"), []string{
+			"Standard OS support is EOL(End-of-Life). Purchase extended support if available or Upgrading your OS is strongly recommended.",
+			"Extended support is also EOL. There are many Vulnerabilities that are not detected, Upgrading your OS strongly recommended.",
+		}},
+		{config.Ubuntu, "18.04.5", date("2023-06-01"), []string{
+			"Standard OS support is EOL(End-of-Life). Purchase extended support if available or Upgrading your OS is strongly recommended.",
+			"Extended support available until 2028-04-30. Check the vendor site.",
+		}},
+		{config.FreeBSD, "11.4", date("2021-06-30"), []string{"Standard OS support will be end in 3 months. EOL date: 2021-09-30"}},
+		{config.FreeBSD, "11", date("2021-09-30"), []string{"Standard OS support will be end in 3 months. EOL date: 2021-09-30"}},
+		{config.FreeBSD, "11", date("2021-06-29"), nil},
+		{config.RedHat, "9", date("2026-01-01"), []string{"Failed to check EOL. Register the issue to https://github.com/future-architect/vuls/issues with the information in 'Family: redhat Release: 9'"}},
+		{config.Amazon, "2 (Karoo)", date("2025-07-01"), []string{"Standard OS support is EOL(End-of-Life). Purchase extended support if available or Upgrading your OS is strongly recommended."}},
+		{config.Amazon, "2018.03", date("2024-01-01"), []string{
+			"Standard OS support is EOL(End-of-Life). Purchase extended support if available or Upgrading your OS is strongly recommended.",
+			"Extended support is also EOL. There are many Vulnerabilities that are not detected, Upgrading your OS strongly recommended.",
+		}},
+		{config.ServerTypePseudo, "", date("2026-01-01"), nil},
+		{config.Raspbian, "10", date("2026-01-01"), nil},
+	}
+	for _, c := range cases {
+		if got := eolWarnings(c.family, c.release, c.now); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, c.want) {
+			t.Errorf("%s %s at %s: got %q, want %q", c.family, c.release, c.now, got, c.want)
+		}
+	}
+}
